newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lower house telcom panel to begin work Wed.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lower house telcom panel to begin work Wed.

text.p: A special committee of Brazil's Chamber of Deputies on Wednesday will begin considering a bill that would open the country's telecommunications sector to private capital, a government-allied whip said.

Deputy Inocencio Oliveira, the lower house leader of the Liberal Front Party (PFL), told reporters the committee would break into three parts to deal with privatization, norms for the sector and the creation of a regulatory body, respectively.

Deputy Paulo Bornhausen of the PFL will serve president of the committee. He will draw up a draft version of legislation governing the privatization of federal telecommunications holding Telebras, Oliveira said.
Deputy Alberto Goldman of the government-allied Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) will be responsible for the parts of the law referring to norms and the regulator, he said.

The government presented a draft of a wide-ranging General Telecommunications Law to Congress in November. It has said it wants the bill approved by April, allowing for the privatization of Telebras to begin this year.
Analysts say 1998 is a more reasonable target for approval of the legislation.
